symbols.name: simultaneous butterfly map
symbols.meaning: The map H_0(u,v) = ((u+v)/2, (u-v)/2) on a pair of values, applied at once to a selected bit of every address chunk.
symbols.quote: The simultaneous butterfly layer $H_0$ is the map $H_0(u,v)=\bigl((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2\bigr)$, applied at once to one selected coordinate bit of every address chunk of an array, where an address chunk is a block of consecutive address bits.

symbols.name: first input value
symbols.meaning: The value at one of the two addresses that differ only in the selected bit.
symbols.quote: A butterfly on one bit takes two values $u$ and $v$ at the two addresses that differ only in that bit, and replaces them by $(u+v)/2$ and $(u-v)/2$.

symbols.name: second input value
symbols.meaning: The value at one of the two addresses that differ only in the selected bit.
symbols.quote: A butterfly on one bit takes two values $u$ and $v$ at the two addresses that differ only in that bit, and replaces them by $(u+v)/2$ and $(u-v)/2$.

symbols.name: selected chunk count
symbols.meaning: The number of address chunks in the layer, each contributing one selected bit.
symbols.quote: The layer uses $D$ chunks, the number of chunks in the layer, each with one selected bit at a common offset from the least significant end.

symbols.name: chunk bound
symbols.meaning: An upper bound on the number of equal-width address chunks in a layer.
symbols.quote: On the layouts used in the multiplication algorithm, one selects the same bit position in each of at most $d$ equal-width address chunks.

symbols.name: logical volume
symbols.meaning: The number of stored data bits in the array.
symbols.quote: Here $V$ is the logical volume, the number of stored data bits.

symbols.name: layer cost exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed exponent below 1 in the cost bound of a layer.
symbols.quote: The layer costs $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, where the exponent $\lambda'<1$ is fixed.

relations.quote: Intermediate values in the layer are exact [Gaussian dyadic numbers](gaussian-dyadic.md), whose real and imaginary parts have power-of-two denominators.
The layer acts on arrays stored in a [frame of a vertex](frame.md) on each wire.
